code:
ZERO = lambda f: lambda x: x
SUCC = lambda n: lambda f: lambda x: f(n(f)(x))

def church_to_int(n):
    return n(lambda x: x + 1)(0)

ONE = SUCC(ZERO)
TWO = SUCC(ONE)
print("church_to_int(ZERO) =", church_to_int(ZERO))
print("church_to_int(ONE)  =", church_to_int(ONE))
print("church_to_int(TWO)  =", church_to_int(TWO))
description: This helper counts a Church numeral's function applications by using Python integer successor and seed zero.

steps.description: ZERO returns its seed unchanged. SUCC wraps one more application of f around a numeral's result.
church_to_int supplies a Python successor function and the seed value 0 to a Church numeral.
ONE applies SUCC to ZERO, and TWO applies SUCC to ONE.

steps.answer: TWO applies it twice, so the seed 0 becomes 2.
steps.question: How many times does TWO apply the supplied successor function?

steps.description: The print calls decode ZERO, ONE, and TWO into their corresponding Python integers.

title: Decode Church numerals
